text:
mel: small but urgent issue from onboarding QA: some sampleapps are emitting full request ids and user emails into structured logs when OTEL_AUTO is enabled. This time the leak comes from our retry wrapper adding a new field `outgoing_req` after redaction runs.

dimitri: can you paste repro? which sample and what build?

mel: multi-lang quickstart, tag onboard-2026-03-29. repro: run the docker sample with `OTEL_AUTO=true` and `LOG_FMT=json`, hit /generate with header `x-request-id: clzdeadbeef0123` and header `user-email: pat@example.com`. Logs captured: the top-level structured log shows `req_id` redacted but a later field `outgoing_req` is unredacted.

harry: saw that too. snippet (redacted manually):
```
{"level":"info","ts":"2026-03-29T15:02:01Z","msg":"recv","req_id":"clz_<redacted>","user":"pat@example.com"}
{"level":"debug","ts":"2026-03-29T15:02:01Z","msg":"retry","outgoing_req":"clzdeadbeef0123","attempt":2}
{"level":"info","ts":"2026-03-29T15:02:01Z","otel":"tracing","trace_id":"a9b8c..."}
```

sam: so the redaction hook runs early and only knows to redact canonical keys. Our retry wrapper (in samples) adds `outgoing_req` later and doesn't use the canonical header name, so it slips through. Also `user` field contains emails in plain text.

mel: QA flagged this as both PII and onboarding leak risk. Security-bot also chimed in.

security-bot: P1 flagged: onboarding artifacts exposing emails and request ids. Recommend pausing public onboarding screenshots until mitigated.

dimitri: proposed immediate steps: 1) flip onboarding images to LOG_FMT=plain and OTEL_AUTO=false for videos; 2) add a small structured logger encoder hook in samples that runs a final pass over JSON payloads and scrubs known patterns and keys (case-insensitive) before printing. This lives in the sample app only as a stop-gap.

harry: for a proper fix we should give SDKs a logger-encoder plugin API so apps and libs can register redaction rules at the final encoding stage. Example API sketch for Node: `logger.addEncoderHook(fn(jsonObj) => sanitizedJsonObj)`. That avoids touching middleware ordering.

sam: +1. If SDKs provide an encoder hook, language parity and default rule set (emails, `clz_` tokens, header variants) will protect apps and third-party libs that add fields later.

mel: short-term PR to samples to add encoder-scrubber: simple rule set: redact any field matching `(?i)(req_id|requestid|outgoing_req|x-request-id)` replace value with `<redacted>`; replace any value matching email regex or `clz_[0-9A-Fa-f]{6,}` with `<redacted>`. I will open it now.

dimitri: also add CI e2e: spin up sample with OTEL_AUTO=true, emit a few requests, capture logs, assert no raw `clz_` or email patterns exist in captured output. Failing that, block publish.

harry: longer term RFC: SDK logger/encoder hooks + `redwood.telemetry.sensitive_fields` configuration shipped by default with common names and patterns. Also include a small performance note: encoder hooks should be optional due to cost on high-throughput hosted paths.

sam: I'll draft the RFC and a minimal Node prototype. mel, pop the PR link in here when done and i'll review the regex to avoid false positives in tests.

mel: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/249 (WIP)
